claim: PRMT7 is associated with human breast cancer metastasis.
source: Arginine methyltransferase PRMT7 is associated with human breast cancer metastasis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known association that provides context for the study.

claim: Endosomal FAK signalling is critical for cancer cell migration.
source: Endosomal FAK signalling is critical for cancer cell migration.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge providing context for the study.

claim: PRMT7 binds to scaffold protein SHANK2.
source: PRMT7 exerted its functions through binding to scaffold protein SHANK2 and catalyzing di-methylation of SHANK2 at R240.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-D demonstrating the interaction between PRMT7 and SHANK2.

claim: PRMT7 catalyzes di-methylation of SHANK2 at R240.
source: PRMT7 exerted its functions through binding to scaffold protein SHANK2 and catalyzing di-methylation of SHANK2 at R240.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 2A and methylation assays in Figures 1G-J and 2C-E.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation exposed ANK domain by disrupting its SPN-ANK domain blockade.
source: SHANK2 R240 methylation exposed ANK domain by disrupting its SPN-ANK domain blockade, promoting in co-accumulation of dynamin2, talin, FAK, cortactin with SHANK2 on endosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulations shown in Figure 4 demonstrating conformational changes.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation promotes co-accumulation of dynamin2, talin, FAK, cortactin with SHANK2 on endosomes.
source: SHANK2 R240 methylation exposed ANK domain by disrupting its SPN-ANK domain blockade, promoting in co-accumulation of dynamin2, talin, FAK, cortactin with SHANK2 on endosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation activated endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vitro.
source: In addition, SHANK2 R240 methylation activated endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data showing increased phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in Figures 6A-G.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation activated endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vivo.
source: In addition, SHANK2 R240 methylation activated endosomal FAK/cortactin signals in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from mouse xenograft models shown in Figure 8.

claim: The levels of PRMT7, methylated SHANK2, FAK Y397 phosphorylation and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation are correlated with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
source: Consistently, all the levels of PRMT7, methylated SHANK2, FAK Y397 phosphorylation and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation were correlated with aggressive clinical breast cancer tissues.
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of 27 human breast cancer specimens shown in Figures 3B-E and Figure 8E-F.

claim: PRMT7 is a type III PRMT that catalyzes mono-methylation of arginine residues on both histone and non-histone substrates.
source: Protein Arginine Methyltransferase 7 (PRMT7) was reported as a type III PRMT to catalyze mono-methylation of arginine residues on both histone and non-histone substrates (Bedford and Clarke, 2009; Karkhanis et al., 2012; Blanc and Richard, 2017; Jain and Clarke, 2019; Haghandish et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PRMT7 can symmetrically di-methylate proteins such as p38 and GLI2.
source: Recent studies also reported that PRMT7 can symmetrically di-methylate proteins such as p38 and GLI2 (Jeong et al., 2020; Vuong et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: PRMT7 promoted metastasis of breast carcinoma cells by triggering EMT program.
source: Specifically, our previous work reported that PRMT7 promoted metastasis of breast carcinoma cells by triggering EMT (epithelial-mesenchymal transition) program (Yao et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: PRMT7 can upregulate the expression of matrix metalloproteinase nine to promote metastasis of breast cancer.
source: PRMT7 can also upregulate the expression of matrix metalloproteinase nine to promote metastasis of breast cancer (Baldwin et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: PRMT7 was automethylated at residue R531, which potentiated the PRMT7-induced EMT program and metastasis.
source: We also found that PRMT7 was automethylated at residue R531, which potentiated the PRMT7-induced EMT program and metastasis (Geng et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Deregulated endocytosis contributes to the acquisition of malignant characteristics in tumour cells, including enhanced cell migration, invasion and metastasis.
source: Increasing evidence indicates that deregulated endocytosis is a relapse mechanism that contributes to the acquisition of malignant characteristics in tumour cells, including enhanced cell migration, invasion and metastasis (Hamidi and Ivaska, 2018; McMahon and Boucrot, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: FAK undergoes autophosphorylation on Y397, which results in cell dissemination.
source: FAK undergos autophosphorylation on Y397, which results in cell dissemination (Alanko et al., 2015; Nader et al., 2016; Xiuping et al., 2018; Hamidi and Ivaska, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Y397 phosphorylation of FAK facilitates the association of FAK with actin-binding protein cortactin.
source: Additionally, Y397 phosphorylation of FAK facilitates the association of FAK with actin-binding protein cortactin, which renders cortactin function in formation of lamellipodia and filopodia (Tomar et al., 2012; Eke et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SHANK2 is associated with multiple proteins including β1-integrin, talin, FAK, EEA1, dynamin2, clathrin, AP2 and cortactin.
source: The mass spectrometric data showed that SHANK2 could interact with numerous endosome associate proteins, including β1-integrin, talin, FAK, EEA1, dynamin2, clathrin, AP2 and cortactin (Figure 5A,B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: PRMT7 is associated with SHANK2, MRPS23, Plectin1, SNRPB and ARHGAP32.
source: The results revealed that PRMT7 is associated with multiple proteins including SHANK2, MRPS23, Plectin1, SNRPB and ARHGAP32.
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The SHANK2 ANK, PDZ and SAM domains are responsible for the interaction between PRMT7 and SHANK2.
source: To map the SHANK2 regions that bind PRMT7, we expressed a series of truncated GST- SHANK2 (Figure 1E), and found that the SHANK2 ANK, PDZ and SAM domains were responsible for the interaction between PRMT7 and SHANK2 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by GST-pulldown assay data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 resulted in increased symmetric arginine di-methylation of SHANK2 in HEK293T cells.
source: By using methylation assay, we found that overexpression of PRMT7 resulted in increased symmetric arginine di-methylation of SHANK2 in HEK293T cells (low level of PRMT7) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: SHANK2 di-methylation level was reduced upon PRMT7 depletion in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: SHANK2 di-methylation level was reduced upon PRMT7 depletion, and the reduced di-methylation of SHANK2 was restored by the reconstituted expression of WT PRMT7 (PRMT7 WT) but not by mutant PRMT7 at its enzymatic domain (PRMT7 Mut) in MDA-MB-231 cells (high level of PRMT7) (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figures 1H and 1I.

claim: The reduced di-methylation of SHANK2 was restored by the reconstituted expression of WT PRMT7 but not by mutant PRMT7 at its enzymatic domain in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: SHANK2 di-methylation level was reduced upon PRMT7 depletion, and the reduced di-methylation of SHANK2 was restored by the reconstituted expression of WT PRMT7 (PRMT7 WT) but not by mutant PRMT7 at its enzymatic domain (PRMT7 Mut) in MDA-MB-231 cells (high level of PRMT7) (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figures 1H and 1I.

claim: Incubation of recombinant PRMT7 and SHANK2 gave rise to a remarkable increase in methylation of SHANK2 in the presence of SAM.
source: Apparently, incubation of recombinant PRMT7 and SHANK2 gave rise to a remarkable increase in methylation of SHANK2 in the presence of SAM, while SHANK2 methylation was undetectable in the absence of SAM (Figure 1J).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro methylation assay data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: SHANK2 methylation was undetectable in the absence of SAM.
source: Apparently, incubation of recombinant PRMT7 and SHANK2 gave rise to a remarkable increase in methylation of SHANK2 in the presence of SAM, while SHANK2 methylation was undetectable in the absence of SAM (Figure 1J).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro methylation assay data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The arginine 240 residue (R240) of SHANK2 was di-methylated.
source: We identified that the arginine 240 residue (R240) of SHANK2 was di-methylated (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The R240 residue of SHANK2 is evolutionarily conserved.
source: Using sequence homology comparison, we found that the R240 residue of SHANK2 is evolutionarily conserved (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Di-methylation level of SHANK2 R240K was lower when compared to SHANK2 WT in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: We found that di-methylation level of SHANK2 R240K was lower when compared to SHANK2 WT in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figures 2C and 2D.

claim: SHANK2 R240 di-methylation level was increased with increasing doses of PRMT7 in HEK293T cells.
source: We then overexpressed increasing doses of PRMT7 in HEK293T cells, and we found that SHANK2 R240 di-methylation level was increased accordingly (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Dosage dependent expression of PRMT5 did not increase the di-methylation at SHANK2 R240.
source: We found that dosage dependent expression of PRMT5 did not increase the di-methylation at SHANK2 R240 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: When PRMT5 activity was inhibited, overexpression of PRMT7 could still increase the SHANK2 di-methylation level both in HEK293T and MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: We found that even when PRMT5 activity was inhibited, overexpression of PRMT7 could still increase the SHANK2 di-methylation level both in HEK293T and MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data with PRMT5 inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Di-methylation of SHANK2 R240 was mainly mediated by PRMT7.
source: Thus, although PRMT5 and PRMT7 existed in the same complex, our data indicated that di-methylation of SHANK2 R240 was mainly mediated by PRMT7.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that PRMT5 inhibition does not prevent PRMT7-mediated SHANK2 methylation.

claim: SHANK2 mRNA was highly expressed in human breast tumours.
source: Consistently, we also observed that SHANK2 mRNA was highly expressed in human breast tumours (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-PCR data from breast cancer tissues shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SHANK2 methylation level was significantly higher in luminal B Her2(+) and Triple-negative breast cancer samples than in normal, luminal A and luminal B Her2(-) samples.
source: The results demonstrated that SHANK2 methylation level was significantly higher in luminal B Her2(+) and Triple-negative breast cancer samples, than that in normal, luminal A and luminal B Her2(-) samples, which implicated a positive correlation between SHANK2 methylation and high metastatic potential (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of human breast cancer samples shown in Figures 3B-E.

claim: There is a positive correlation between SHANK2 methylation and high metastatic potential.
source: The results demonstrated that SHANK2 methylation level was significantly higher in luminal B Her2(+) and Triple-negative breast cancer samples, than that in normal, luminal A and luminal B Her2(-) samples, which implicated a positive correlation between SHANK2 methylation and high metastatic potential (Figure 3B–E).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that SHANK2 methylation is higher in more aggressive breast cancer subtypes.

claim: Among 1075 breast cancer patients, 89 out of 847 PRMT7 low-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (10.5%).
source: Among 1075 breast cancer patients, 89 out of 847 PRMT7 low-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (10.5%), while 63 out of 228 PRMT7 high-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (27.6%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 63 out of 228 PRMT7 high-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (27.6%).
source: Among 1075 breast cancer patients, 89 out of 847 PRMT7 low-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (10.5%), while 63 out of 228 PRMT7 high-expression breast cancer patients were stage III or IV (27.6%) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by TCGA database analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The expression of PRMT7 was positively correlated with the proportion of patients with stage III or IV breast cancer.
source: These data indicated that the expression of PRMT7 was positively correlated with the proportion of patients with stage III or IV breast cancer, which predicted poor prognosis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the TCGA database analysis showing higher proportion of advanced stage cancer in PRMT7 high-expression patients.

claim: High metastatic potential breast cancer cells (BT549 and MDA-MB-231) exhibited high SHANK2 di-methylation levels.
source: Out of 6 cell lines analyzed, high metastatic potential breast cancer cells (BT549 and MDA-MB-231) exhibited high SHANK2 di-methylation levels, whereas normal mammary epithelial cell (MCF10A), low metastatic potential breast cancer cell (MCF7, BT474 and T47D) showed relatively low SHANK2 di-methylation level (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-PCR and western blot data from multiple cell lines shown in Figures 3F and 3G.

claim: Normal mammary epithelial cell (MCF10A) and low metastatic potential breast cancer cells (MCF7, BT474 and T47D) showed relatively low SHANK2 di-methylation level.
source: Out of 6 cell lines analyzed, high metastatic potential breast cancer cells (BT549 and MDA-MB-231) exhibited high SHANK2 di-methylation levels, whereas normal mammary epithelial cell (MCF10A), low metastatic potential breast cancer cell (MCF7, BT474 and T47D) showed relatively low SHANK2 di-methylation level (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-PCR and western blot data from multiple cell lines shown in Figures 3F and 3G.

claim: The epithelial marker ZO-1 was increased upon SHANK2 depletion.
source: Furthermore, we analyzed the expression profile of EMT-associated markers, and found that the epithelial marker ZO-1 was increased, while the mesenchymal markers Fibronectin and N-cadherin were decreased upon SHANK2 depletion
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The mesenchymal markers Fibronectin and N-cadherin were decreased upon SHANK2 depletion.
source: Furthermore, we analyzed the expression profile of EMT-associated markers, and found that the epithelial marker ZO-1 was increased, while the mesenchymal markers Fibronectin and N-cadherin were decreased upon SHANK2 depletion
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: ZO-1 expression was decreased while Fibronectin and N-cadherin expressions were restored by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells.
source: meanwhile, ZO-1 expression was decreased while Fibronectin and N-cadherin expressions were restored by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells (Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3H and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: MMP2/MMP9 activation was inhibited by SHANK2 depletion.
source: In addition, MMP2/MMP9 activation was inhibited by SHANK2 depletion, while the inhibition was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K (Figure 3I)
evidence: This claim is supported by gelatin zymography data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The inhibition of MMP2/MMP9 activation was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K.
source: In addition, MMP2/MMP9 activation was inhibited by SHANK2 depletion, while the inhibition was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K (Figure 3I)
evidence: This claim is supported by gelatin zymography data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: The migration/invasion capabilities of MDA-MB-231 cells were inhibited by SHANK2 depletion.
source: and the migration/invasion capabilities of MDA-MB-231 cells were also inhibited by SHANK2 depletion, and in both cases the inhibition was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K (Figure 3J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by transwell migration and invasion assay data shown in Figures 3J and 3K.

claim: The inhibition of migration/invasion capabilities was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K.
source: and the migration/invasion capabilities of MDA-MB-231 cells were also inhibited by SHANK2 depletion, and in both cases the inhibition was abrogated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K (Figure 3J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by transwell migration and invasion assay data shown in Figures 3J and 3K.

claim: The SPN domain in Dimethyl R240 needs less energy to reach an 'open' state than that in SHANK2 WT and R240K.
source: As shown in Figure 4A, the SPN domain in Dimethyl R240 needs less energy to reach an 'open' state than that in SHANK2 WT and R240K, according to the free energy profile.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: R240 can form hydrogen bonds with its neighbouring residue H236.
source: R240 can form hydrogen bonds with its neighbouring residue H236 and by this R240 remotely influences the interactions between SPN and ANK via hydrogen bond network (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: R240 methylation dramatically decreased interactions between R240 and H236.
source: It indicates that R240 methylation dramatically decreased interactions between R240 and H236.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the structural analysis of hydrogen bonding patterns.

claim: R240 methylation weakened the stability of the closed state of SHANK2.
source: It further weakened the stability of the closed state of SHANK2.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the molecular dynamics simulation results showing decreased energy barrier for opening.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation disrupted SPN-ANK domain blockade to 'open' SHANK2, providing more chances for insertion of partner proteins.
source: Thus, structural analyses suggest that SHANK2 R240 methylation disrupted SPN-ANK domain blockade to 'open' SHANK2, providing more chances for insertion of partner proteins.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the molecular dynamics simulation and structural analysis data.

claim: Talin, FAK, dynamin2, cortactin and SHANK2 were in the same complex in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: To test this hypothesis, we first verified the mass spec data by using CoIP assays and we confirmed that talin, FAK, dynamin2, cortactin and SHANK2 were in the same complex in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 promoted the co-precipitation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2 with cortactin in MCF7 cells.
source: We found that overexpression of PRMT7 promoted the co-precipitation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2 with cortactin in MCF7 cells, and the interaction was reduced in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figures 5D and 5F.

claim: The interaction of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2 with cortactin was reduced in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: We found that overexpression of PRMT7 promoted the co-precipitation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2 with cortactin in MCF7 cells, and the interaction was reduced in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figures 5D and 5F.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 triggered an accumulation in the number of EEA1-positive endosomes with more talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 colocalization in MCF7 cells.
source: Additionally, overexpression of PRMT7 triggered an accumulation in the number of EEA1-positive endosomes with more talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 colocalization in MCF7 cells, and the colocalization was attenuated in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5E and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 5E and 5G.

claim: The colocalization of talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 was attenuated in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Additionally, overexpression of PRMT7 triggered an accumulation in the number of EEA1-positive endosomes with more talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 colocalization in MCF7 cells, and the colocalization was attenuated in PRMT7 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5E and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 5E and 5G.

claim: The formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin was significantly increased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Consistently, the formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin was significantly increased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: SHANK2 WT promoted the recruitment of EEA1-positive endosomes and the majority of SHANK2 was associated with endosome associate proteins.
source: Meanwhile, SHANK2 WT promoted the recruitment of EEA1-positive endosomes and the majority of SHANK2 was associated with endosome associate proteins, which was significantly reduced by SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells (Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The association of SHANK2 with endosome proteins was significantly reduced by SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells.
source: Meanwhile, SHANK2 WT promoted the recruitment of EEA1-positive endosomes and the majority of SHANK2 was associated with endosome associate proteins, which was significantly reduced by SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 and BT549 cells (Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5I and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The interaction of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin was enhanced by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240K in MCF10A cells expressing low level of PRMT7.
source: Consistent with this finding, the interaction of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin and the localization between talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 with endosome compartment was enhanced by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F (as a methyl-mimic) but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240K in MCF10A cells expressing low level of PRMT7 (Figure 5J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 5J and 5K.

claim: The localization between talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 with endosome compartment was enhanced by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240K in MCF10A cells expressing low level of PRMT7.
source: Consistent with this finding, the interaction of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin and the localization between talin, FAK, EEA1 and dynamin2 with endosome compartment was enhanced by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F (as a methyl-mimic) but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240K in MCF10A cells expressing low level of PRMT7 (Figure 5J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 5J and 5K.

claim: SHANK2 silencing partially reduced the formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin complex in PRMT7-MCF7 cells.
source: SHANK2 silencing partially reduced the formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin complex (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A) and markedly decreased the interaction between talin and FAK (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: SHANK2 silencing markedly decreased the interaction between talin and FAK in PRMT7-MCF7 cells.
source: SHANK2 silencing partially reduced the formation of dynamin2/talin/FAK/SHANK2/cortactin complex (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A) and markedly decreased the interaction between talin and FAK (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT7 markedly increased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MCF7 cells.
source: As expected, overexpression of PRMT7 markedly increased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MCF7 cells, and PRMT7 depletion profoundly decreased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: PRMT7 depletion profoundly decreased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: As expected, overexpression of PRMT7 markedly increased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MCF7 cells, and PRMT7 depletion profoundly decreased FAK and cortactin phosphorylation in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: FAK and cortactin were activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K.
source: Consistently, FAK and cortactin were activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data showing phosphorylation levels in Figure 6C.

claim: Blocking FAK activation with FAK inhibitor GSK2256098 inhibited phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin upregulated by SHANK2 R240F in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Furthermore, blocking FAK activation with FAK inhibitor GSK2256098 did inhibit phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin upregulated by SHANK2 R240F in SHANK2 depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data with FAK inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Treatment with dynasore decreased SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Treatment with dynasore or silencing of EEA1 greatly decreased SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 6F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data with dynasore treatment shown in Figures 6F and 6G.

claim: Silencing of EEA1 greatly decreased SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Treatment with dynasore or silencing of EEA1 greatly decreased SHANK2 R240F induced-phosphorylation of FAK and cortactin in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 6F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data with EEA1 knockdown shown in Figures 6F and 6G.

claim: Treatment with dynasore decreased PRMT7 induced-EMT program in MCF7 cells.
source: Indeed, treatment with dynasore decreased PRMT7 induced-EMT program and migration/invasion capabilities of MCF7 cells (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Treatment with dynasore decreased PRMT7 induced-migration/invasion capabilities of MCF7 cells.
source: Indeed, treatment with dynasore decreased PRMT7 induced-EMT program and migration/invasion capabilities of MCF7 cells (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by transwell assay data shown in Figures 7B and 7C.

claim: EMT and cell migration/invasion were activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F or SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Likewise, EMT and cell migration/invasion were activated by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240F or SHANK2 WT but not of SHANK2 R240K in SHANK2-depleted MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot and transwell assay data shown in Figures 7D-F.

claim: Dynasore dramatically inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: To determine the functional role of SHANK2 R240 methylation is dependent on endocytosis, we treated SHANK2 R240F MDA-MB-231 cells with dynasore, and found that dynasore dramatically inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Dynasore dramatically inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-cell migration/invasion in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: To determine the functional role of SHANK2 R240 methylation is dependent on endocytosis, we treated SHANK2 R240F MDA-MB-231 cells with dynasore, and found that dynasore dramatically inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by transwell assay data shown in Figures 7E and 7F.

claim: Knockdown of EEA1 markedly reduced SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Similarly, knockdown of EEA1 also markedly reduced SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion (Figure 7G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Knockdown of EEA1 markedly reduced SHANK2 R240F induced-cell migration/invasion in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Similarly, knockdown of EEA1 also markedly reduced SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion (Figure 7G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by transwell assay data shown in Figures 7H and 7I.

claim: GSK2256098 inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Since SHANK2 R240 methylation promotes cell migration/invasion through activating endosomal FAK signalling, we treated SHANK2 R240F MDA-MB-231 cells with FAK inhibitor GSK2256098, and found that GSK2256098 also inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion (Figure 7J–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7J.

claim: GSK2256098 inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-cell migration/invasion in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Since SHANK2 R240 methylation promotes cell migration/invasion through activating endosomal FAK signalling, we treated SHANK2 R240F MDA-MB-231 cells with FAK inhibitor GSK2256098, and found that GSK2256098 also inhibited the effects of SHANK2 R240F induced-EMT and cell migration/invasion (Figure 7J–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by transwell assay data shown in Figures 7K and 7L (referenced but not shown in manuscript excerpt).

claim: Lung metastases and the number of metastatic pulmonary nodules were dramatically decreased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240K, but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240F.
source: The results demonstrated that lung metastases and the number of metastatic pulmonary nodules were dramatically decreased by reconstituted expression of SHANK2 R240K, but not of SHANK2 WT or SHANK2 R240F (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The mice injected with SHANK2 R240F cells and treated with GSK2256098 formed fewer lung metastatic foci than that injected with SHANK2 R240F.
source: We also discovered that the mice injected with SHANK2 R240F cells and treated with GSK2256098 formed fewer lung metastatic foci than that injected with SHANK2 R240F (Figure 8B).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo xenograft data with FAK inhibitor treatment shown in Figure 8B.

claim: SHANK2 R240F expression reinforced FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation in vivo.
source: In addition, immunohistochemistry staining results indicated that SHANK2 R240F expression reinforced FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation, whereas SHANK2 R240F with GSK2256098 treatment profoundly inhibited SHANK2 R240F induced-FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation (Figure 8C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from xenograft tumors shown in Figures 8C and 8D.

claim: SHANK2 R240F with GSK2256098 treatment profoundly inhibited SHANK2 R240F induced-FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation in vivo.
source: In addition, immunohistochemistry staining results indicated that SHANK2 R240F expression reinforced FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation, whereas SHANK2 R240F with GSK2256098 treatment profoundly inhibited SHANK2 R240F induced-FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation (Figure 8C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data from xenograft tumors shown in Figures 8C and 8D.

claim: There is a correlation among PRMT7, FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation levels, and the clinical aggressiveness of breast cancer.
source: Immunohistochemistry staining results revealed a correlation among PRMT7, FAK Y397 and cortactin Y421 phosphorylation levels, and the clinical aggressiveness of breast cancer (Figure 8E,F and Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry analysis of 27 human breast cancer specimens shown in Figures 8E, 8F and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: SHANK3 SPN domain interacts with the ANK domain in an intramolecular manner, thereby restricting access of either Sharpin or α-fodrin.
source: A previous study reported that SHANK3 SPN domain interacts with the ANK domain in an intramolecular manner, thereby restricting access of either Sharpin or α-fodrin (Mameza et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: SHANK1 and SHANK3 were reported to inhibit cell spreading, migration and invasion in cancer cells through sequestering active Rap1 and R-Ras.
source: SHANK1 and SHANK3 were reported to inhibit cell spreading, migration and invasion in cancer cells through sequestering active Rap1 and R-Ras (Lilja et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Dynamin is best known for its role in catalyzing membrane scission at late stages of clathrin-mediated endocytosis to release clathrin-coated vesicles into the cytosol.
source: Dynamin is best known for its role in catalyzing membrane scission at late stages of clathrin-mediated endocytosis to release clathrin-coated vesicles into the cytosol (Kaksonen and Roux, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Dynamin can regulate earlier stages of endosome maturation through binding the scaffold protein EEA1.
source: Furthermore, increasing evidence suggests that dynamin can also regulate earlier stages of endosome maturation through binding the scaffold protein EEA1, in turn regulate the recruitment of other factors to the membrane that control endosomal sorting and maturation (Hamidi and Ivaska, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: PRMT7 promoted dynamin2 interaction with methylated SHANK2.
source: Our results demonstrated that PRMT7 promoted dynamin2 interaction with methylated SHANK2 (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: The PRMT7-mediated SHANK2 methylation rendered EEA1 to co-localize with SHANK2.
source: Moreover, the PRMT7-mediated SHANK2 methylation rendered EEA1 to co-localize with SHANK2 (Figure 5I).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 might enhance the activity of dynamin2 and thus regulate the formation of endosome.
source: These results indicate that methylated SHANK2 might enhance the activity of dynamin2 and thus regulate the formation of endosome.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental observations of protein interactions and colocalization.

claim: SHANK family proteins are able to bind and interact with a wide range of proteins including actin binding proteins and actin modulators, such as dynamin2, cortactin, RICH2, and PIX.
source: Scaffold proteins SHANK1, 2, three are able to bind and interact with a wide range of proteins including actin binding proteins and actin modulators, such as dynamin2, cortactin, RICH2, and PIX (Lee et al., 2010; Sheng and Kim, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SHANK1 and SHANK3 acted as negative regulators of integrin activity by binding R-Ras, thereby inhibiting migration and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Recent studies reported that SHANK1 and SHANK3 acted as negative regulators of integrin activity by binding R-Ras, thereby inhibiting migration and invasion of MDA-MB-231 cells (Lilja et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 was correlated with high level of incidence of breast cancer.
source: In contrast to SHANK1 and SHANK3, the present study revealed that SHANK2, especially the methylated SHANK2, was correlated with high level of incidence of breast cancer (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot analysis of breast cancer samples shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 promoted breast cancer metastasis.
source: Our data demonstrated that methylated SHANK2 promoted breast cancer metastasis (Figure 8A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vivo xenograft data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 could bind to receptor proteins, including integrin, Met, NRP1 and EGFR.
source: Like SHANK3, our mass spectrometry results demonstrated that methylated SHANK2 could bind to receptor proteins, not only integrin but also Met, NRP1 and EGFR, which indicated that PRMT7-SHANK2 might be involved in receptor mediated endocytosis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: PRMT7-SHANK2 might be involved in receptor mediated endocytosis.
source: Like SHANK3, our mass spectrometry results demonstrated that methylated SHANK2 could bind to receptor proteins, not only integrin but also Met, NRP1 and EGFR, which indicated that PRMT7-SHANK2 might be involved in receptor mediated endocytosis (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the mass spectrometry data showing interactions with receptor proteins.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 could interact with relative endomembrane organelles marker, such as EEA1, LAMP1, Calnexin, GOLM1, Ninein, CD63, TOM70 and LanminA/C.
source: In our study, we also demonstrated that methylated SHANK2 could interact with relative endomembrane organelles marker, such as EEA1, LAMP1, Calnexin, GOLM1, Ninein, CD63, TOM70 and LanminA/C (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SHANK2 could localize not only on endosomes but also on lysosome, mitochondria, ER, Golgi, centrosome, exosome and nuclear.
source: These results indicated that SHANK2 could localize not only on endosomes but also on lysosome, mitochondria, ER, Golgi, centrosome, exosome and nuclear.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the mass spectrometry data showing interactions with various organelle markers.

claim: The methylated SHANK2 was co-localized with several common exosome marker proteins, including CD63 and CD81.
source: Indeed, we found that the methylated SHANK2 was co-localized with several common exosome marker proteins, including CD63 and CD81 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A).

claim: SHANK2 WT promoted recruitment of EEA1-positive endosomes and co-localized more CD63 and CD81 than that of SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 cells.
source: Meanwhile, SHANK2 WT promoted recruitment of EEA1-positive endosomes and co-localized more CD63 and CD81 than that of SHANK2 R240K in MDA-MB-231 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The PRMT7-SHANK2 might be secreted by exosomes and continuously internalized and sustained the active talin/FAK/cortactin complexes on endosomes.
source: Thus, it is likely that the PRMT7-SHANK2 might be secreted by exosomes and continuously internalized and sustained the active talin/FAK/cortactin complexes on endosomes, and thereby provided persistent endosomal signals for tumour progression.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the observed colocalization with exosome markers.

claim: PRMT7-dependent SHANK2 methylation is a key player in mediating endosomal FAK signals activation.
source: These findings characterize the PRMT7-dependent SHANK2 methylation as a key player in mediating endosomal FAK signals activation
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from the collective experimental data presented in the study.

claim: SHANK2 R240 methylation has value as a target for breast cancer metastasis.
source: also point to the value of SHANK2 R240 methylation as a target for breast cancer metastasis.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the findings that SHANK2 R240 methylation promotes metastasis.

claim: Methylated SHANK2 might be a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer development.
source: As a key player in breast cancer development, methylated SHANK2 might be a potential therapeutic target.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the role of methylated SHANK2 in promoting breast cancer metastasis.
